test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 1 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Rukmini Devi Arundale was a dancer of which of the following classical Indian dance forms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale:**

 
 
• She **was an Indian theosophist**, **dancer, **and **choreographer **of the Indian classical dance **form of Bharatanatyam.**
 
• She was an **activist for animal welfare**.
 
• She was the **first woman in Indian history **to be **nominated **as a **member of the Rajya Sabha**, the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• **Rukmini Devi's pedagogy **is what led to her **creation of dance**.
 
• She **practically changed how Bharatanatyam **and **Indian "traditional" dance are learned**, **taught**, and **performed throughout India **and the rest of the globe by building an institution, **"Kalakshetra," **around it.
 
 
 
• A **significant type of Indian classical dance **that has its **roots in Tamil Nadu is Bharatanatyam**. The dance **style is briefly described **as **"Bharata Natya" **in Someshwara III's Kannada work **Manasollasa**. Since **ancient times**, it has **flourished in the temples and courts of southern India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A significant ancient Indian classical dance**, known as **Odissi **in **older writings**, has its roots in the **temples of Odisha**, an eastern **coastal state of India**.
 
• **Music**, **dance**, **theatre**, and **other linked disciplines **are **all included in **the body of work known as **Sattriya dance **and theatre. These **artistic disciplines are extremely important to Assamese spiritual and social life**.
 
• A **significant type of classical Indian dance is kathakali**. The extremely **colourful make-up, costumes, and face masks **that the traditionally **male actor-dancers **wear set this **"story play" kind of art apart**. It is indigenous to Kerala's Malayalam-speaking southwest region, where Malayalis predominately practise and enjoy it.
